findings.claim: init now writes a surface eject cannot remove and does not even name. scrubClaudeSkills is anchored at `.claude/skills` (eject.ts:638) and the dirty-tree roster is the `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` literal only (eject.ts:1133, locked by eject.test.ts:1997) — neither file mentions `.agents`. The docblock this diff invalidates is eject.ts:631-633 ('a new distributed skill can never orphan on eject because a hand-mirrored list drifted'): the diff creates that orphan class on the ROOT dimension, and no gate catches it.
findings.counterexample: Executed in a temp repo (git init, CLAUDE.md, empty .agents/): initCommand({yes:true}) then ejectCommand({force:true}). POST-INIT .claude/skills and .agents/skills both hold review-loop, review-reply, signoff, signon; POST-EJECT .claude/skills = ABSENT, .agents/skills still holds all four. Eject printed 'Totem has been ejected from this project.' and its Removed/Skipped lists named only .claude/skills/*.

findings.claim: The stated predicate is wrong in the direction that matters. The docs say the twin is written 'where the repository carries an .agents/ directory'; the real predicate is that AND Claude Code detected, because the writer is reached only through installClaudeHooks (init.ts:918; detection init-detect.ts:178). The .agents/skills surface is the VENDOR-NEUTRAL one (doctor-parity.ts:218-221; parity-manifest vendor-adapter: gemini, agy, kimi, codex), so the population that most needs it is the population the fix skips.
findings.counterexample: Executed initCommand({yes:true}) on three temp repos. (A) CLAUDE.md + .agents/: all eight skill rows, twins written. (B) CLAUDE.md, no .agents/: the one skipped row. (C) .gemini/ + .agents/, no Claude surface: 'Detected AI tools: Gemini CLI', writes .gemini/skills/totem.md and NOTHING else — .claude/skills = ABSENT, .agents/skills = ABSENT, and no skipped row explains why.

findings.claim: 'as a byte-equal twin on every run' overclaims against the contract the twin carries: managed-block equality with a per-surface extension tail (parity-manifest.yaml:285-287 'byte-equality there is the zero-extension case, not the contract'; mmnto-ai/totem#2788's Ask 'preserves each surface's own extension tail outside the markers'). The changeset repeats it, and the new test locks byte equality on a zero-tail fixture only. The code is right; the prose and the release note are wrong.

findings.claim: Every .agents row renders in the install summary as 'Scaffolded Claude Code hook' — the vendor-neutral surface labelled with the vendor it exists to be neutral about, and a skill labelled a hook (init.ts:1982 `summaryActionOverride ?? Scaffolded ${tool.name} hook`). The skipped row prints with a green OK glyph BEFORE the four .claude skill rows because it is pushed ahead of the loop.
findings.counterexample: Executed initCommand({yes:true}) summary, fixture A: 'OK .agents/skills/signoff/SKILL.md — Scaffolded Claude Code hook' (and the same for the other three). Fixture B: 'OK .agents/skills/ (twins) — Skipped: no .agents/ directory in this repository …' printed first.

findings.claim: fs.existsSync(path.join(cwd, '.agents')) is a presence test, not a directory test; an .agents that is a FILE passes it and then fails four times inside scaffoldClaudeSkill's catch, and initCommand routes err rows to log.error, never the summary, so init prints 'Init complete' over four 'Totem Error' lines. fs.statSync(...).isDirectory() would make the file case one honest skipped row.
findings.counterexample: Executed: .agents as a file → four rows 'skipped .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md ERR=[Totem Error] ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdir …', the four .claude copies created, the .agents file untouched. Read-only stale twin (chmod 0444): 'skipped … ERR=[Totem Error] EPERM', the stale twin survives the run.

findings.claim: The skipped row's wording asserts a repository-level fact from a cwd-level probe ('no .agents/ directory in this repository'); cwd is process.cwd(), not the git root (doctor-parity anchors its equivalent read at the git root, doctor-parity.ts:848-850). Run from a package subdirectory of a repo that carries .agents/, the line is false as written and the twins silently go unrefreshed.
findings.counterexample: Executed: temp root with .agents/skills/ present, distributeClaudeSkills(<root>/packages/app) → row 'skipped .agents/skills/ (twins) … no .agents/ directory in this repository', while 'repo root .agents exists: true' and 'twins written under subdir: false'.
